Klappvisors V. 26.1 2/13

__ 1. Implementation

The document has been created and approved by the General Assembly of 09.11.2024.
The document and its rules have been implemented since the 2025 season.

2. Definition

Klappvisor Bascinet is a medieval helmet that originated in the 14th century.
"Klappvisor" is German and translates to "folding visor."
The single brow-mounted hinge is a distinctive feature of early bascinet visor designs.

These bascinet visors were often low profile to fit underneath a great helm, but would also serve as a
primary defense on their own.

Klappvisor uses a solid metal visor to protect the face, attached on the forehead by a piece of metal, the
“spoon”.
Klappvisor was used from 1340 to 1400, mainly in Germany and Italy.

Klappvisor is Approved for 14th century and Transitional armors.

Klappvisor is Denied for 15th century armors.

__ 4. Requirements

4.1. General Requirements

Reproductions must closely resemble the appearance and proportions of a Klappvisor source.

Any metal part of the helmet must conform to the “Armors and Weapons Aesthetics and Decorations”
document.

Any textile or leather part of the helmet must conform to the “Textiles and Leather” document.

4.2. Visor

Visors must not be too long or too short, it must respect the proportions of historical sources.
The hinge must be reproduced as per historical sources.

It is Allowed to weld the hinge. Welded hinges must resemble a functional hinge.

It is Allowed to weld the visor down. Welded visors must resemble a functional removable visor.

It is Allowed to add a metal plate to protect the throat. Such a plate must be strong enough to endure full
contact fight and must be concealed under the Aventail.

A leather strap can be used to secure the visor down.

Breath holes should be round and must not exceed a diameter of 10mm. Breath holes must not be so
numerous that they compromise the helm’s structural integrity. It is acceptable to mirror breath holes to
both sides.

Breath holes of another shape must be documented by historical sources to be allowed.

4.3. Eye Slots

Eye slots should resemble sources for the visor.
Eye slots should not exceed 25mm tall to prevent any injury.
Klappvisor with 2 Eye slots are allowed to add up to two (2) safety Eye bars per Eye slot.

Klappvisor may have integrated Eye bars. Such Eye bars must be made accordingly with historical
sources, in terms of proportion, numbers and aesthetic.

Externally riveted Eye bars are not allowed.
Eye bars must conform to the “Eye bars” document.

4.4. Aventail

Klappvisors must be worn with chainmail Aventails, fabric Aventails, or scales Aventails.
Aventails must conform to the “Aventails” document.
Aventails must be attached to the bascinet by a system of leather and vervelles.

Chainmail Aventail must be fastened down to the edge of a padded pelerine, attached to the helmet
liner.

Scales and Fabric Aventails are recommended to be fastened down to the edge of a padded pelerine,
attached to the helmet liner.

Any additional protective plates covering the cervical spine must be hidden under the Aventail.

4.5. Others

Klappvisors may be decorated in the spirit of medieval styles, such as orle, torse, decorated Aventails
(with copper/brass chainmail rings), vervelle covers and coat of arms badges etc.

Such decoration must be made in coherence with historical sources.
Using modern and/or offensive imagery and slogans is prohibited.
